title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ipv6: raw: fix use-after-free in rawv6_send_hdrinc() rawv6_send_hdrinc() caches the route before handing the…
desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv6: raw: fix use-after-free in rawv6_send_hdrinc()

rawv6_send_hdrinc() caches the route before handing the skb to
l3mdev_ip6_out(). The VRF output path may replace skb->dst and release
the original route, leaving the cached pointer stale.

The function later dereferences that pointer for statistics accounting
and as the output device passed to NF_HOOK(). Its RCU read-side critical
section starts after l3mdev_ip6_out(), so it cannot prevent the old route
from being reclaimed in between.

Reload the route from the current skb destination after
l3mdev_ip6_out() returns.

KASAN reports a slab-use-after-free in rawv6_sendmsg(), with the route
allocated by ip6_dst_alloc(), freed by dst_destroy() from rcu_core(), and
the related RCU callback queued from vrf_l3_out().

title: In Eclipse iceoryx-rs, versions 0.0.11 to 0.0.13 and 0.1.0 as well as on the latest main branch.
desc:
In Eclipse iceoryx-rs, versions 0.0.11 to 0.0.13 and 0.1.0 as well as on the latest main branch.



`SampleReceiver::<T>::take()` and `Sample::<T>::deref()` are safe functions that hand the caller a `&T` pointing at a chunk written by another iceoryx process, but the subscriber path neither requires `T: ShmSend` nor verifies that the received chunk is at least `size_of::<T>()` bytes / `align_of::<T>()`-aligned. A peer process that publishes an undersized chunk, or any chunk at all when the subscriber chose a pointer-bearing `T`, drives a `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` subscriber into out-of-bounds reads of adjacent shared-memory chunks or dereference of a publisher-controlled pointer.



Resolution:



It will not be fixed since this is a known limitation in iceoryx as it is the users responsibility to specify the same data type on sender and receiver side.



[iceoryx2](https://github.com/eclipse-iceoryx/iceoryx2) is the successor of iceoryx-rs where the API is designed to prevent this by default.



It is strongly recommended to migrate to iceoryx2 which is actively maintained and receives security support.



The iceoryx-rs package has officially reached End-of-life and will not receive any features, bugfixes or security fixes.

title: Deco BE65 firmware contains a cryptographic weakness in the local web-management authentication flow due to the use of insufficient RSA key sizes.
desc:
Deco BE65 firmware contains a cryptographic weakness in the local web-management authentication flow due to the use of insufficient RSA key sizes. The /login?form=auth endpoint returns a 512-bit RSA public key and sequence value. 

Successful exploitation may compromise the cryptographic protections applied to local web-management authentication traffic.

title: The Deco BE65 v3 firmware contains a shared hard-coded password hash for the root account in /etc/shadow.
desc:
The Deco BE65 v3 firmware contains a shared hard-coded password hash for the root account in /etc/shadow. Where the corresponding credential is accepted by a production authentication path, an attacker with existing unprivileged shell access may recover or otherwise obtain the plaintext password and use it to escalate privileges. 

Successful exploitation may grant root-level access to the affected device.

title: When Private data source connect (PDC) or a secure SOCKS proxy is used, the MQTT data source plugin does not apply TLS to broker connections for the tls, ssl, tcps, mqtts and…
desc: When Private data source connect (PDC) or a secure SOCKS proxy is used, the MQTT data source plugin does not apply TLS to broker connections for the tls, ssl, tcps, mqtts and mqtt+ssl schemes. The configured TLS settings are ignored, and the broker username and password are sent unencrypted on the hop between the proxy and the broker. The server certificate is not verified, and a configured client certificate is not sent.

title: The WP Duplicate – WordPress Migration Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Missing Authorization in versions up to, and including, 1.1.11.
desc: The WP Duplicate – WordPress Migration Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Missing Authorization in versions up to, and including, 1.1.11. This is due to a missing capability check and missing nonce check on the start_zip_creation, start_zip_download, local_sync_get_init_root_files, and local_sync_get_files_by_key AJAX actions in the start_zip_creation_dev() and sibling functions. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to overwrite the plugin's prod_site_url setting so it points at an attacker-controlled host and enumerate arbitrary server directories, which when combined with a subsequent administrator-triggered sync results in an unsigned attacker-supplied ZIP archive being fetched, extracted via a WordPress-independent bridge deployed under the web root, resulting in remote code execution on the affected site.

title: The Foxtool All-in-One: Contact chat button, Custom login, Media optimize images plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'foxtool_image_id'…
desc: The Foxtool All-in-One: Contact chat button, Custom login, Media optimize images plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'foxtool_image_id' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.5.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. A subscriber-level attacker can store a payload in their own profile's foxtoolpic user-meta that executes in an administrator's browser session when the administrator views the user via the Users → Edit screen.

title: The NextScripts: Social Networks Auto-Poster plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'comment_author' and 'comment_agent' Comment Fields in all…
desc: The NextScripts: Social Networks Auto-Poster plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'comment_author' and 'comment_agent' Comment Fields in all versions up to, and including, 4.4.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The injected payload executes in an administrator's browser session when the administrator views the WordPress comment moderation queue, including pending and unapproved comments, meaning no prior approval of the comment is required for exploitation.

title: The device only supports Wi-Fi protocols vulnerable to deauthentication attacks (WEP/WPA/WPA2).
desc:
The device only supports Wi-Fi protocols vulnerable to
deauthentication attacks (WEP/WPA/WPA2). Should any event which would typically
be logged to the user’s mobile device (such as arming or disarming the alarm or
any tamper events) be incurred whilst the device is temporarily disconnected
from its Wi-Fi network (such as via a deauthentication attack), those alerts
will not be sent even after connection is regained.

title: The static codes used for information transmission throughout the 433.92 MHz system of the Guardian 2 system allow an attacker in proximity to monitor the movements of users…
desc:
The static codes used for information transmission
throughout the 433.92 MHz system of the Guardian 2 system allow an attacker in
proximity to monitor the movements of users inside the premises where the
sensors are set up. This is further aided by the fact that codes transmitted
reveal sensor type, although sensor location cannot be inferred from this
traffic alone.

title: The Guardian 2 alarm unit lacks a mechanism to authenticate control commands sent over 433.92 MHz, which allows an attacker to replay the static commands to impersonate activity.
desc:
The Guardian 2 alarm unit lacks a mechanism to
authenticate control commands sent over 433.92 MHz, which allows an attacker to
replay the static commands to impersonate activity.  The attacker can also disarm or arm the
system at will if a Nexsmart keypad (product link) is in use, thus compromising
the functionality of the alarm system completely.

title: PGPainless is a simple-to-use OpenPGP API based on Bouncy Castle.
desc: PGPainless is a simple-to-use OpenPGP API based on Bouncy Castle. Prior to 1.7.8 and from 2.0.0 until 2.0.4, pgpainless-sop/src/main/kotlin/org/pgpainless/sop/InlineDetachImpl.kt InlineDetachImpl and pgpainless-core/src/main/kotlin/org/pgpainless/decryption_verification/MessageInspector.kt MessageInspector manually descend PGPCompressedData packets without incrementing or enforcing MAX_LAYER_DEPTH. A remote unauthenticated attacker can supply an untrusted OpenPGP message containing deeply nested compressed packet structures to a downstream application using inline-detach or message inspection, bypass the intended 16-layer limit, and force continued decompression and packet processing. The resulting resource consumption can block processing threads, exhaust heap memory, and crash the consuming application. This issue is fixed in versions 1.7.8 and 2.0.4.

title: Miren Runtime provides the runtime component for the Miren application platform.
desc: Miren Runtime provides the runtime component for the Miren application platform. Prior to 0.11.1, the QUIC/HTTP3 RPC server on the default port 8443 uses tls.RequestClientCert and does not verify that presented certificates chain to the configured cluster certificate authority. The RPC authenticators derive a caller identity from PeerCertificates[0].Subject.CommonName without requiring a non-empty VerifiedChains value, and certificate identities bypass all RBAC checks. A network attacker who can reach the listener can present a self-signed certificate with an issuer distinguished name matching the public cluster CA subject and gain cluster superuser access, allowing disclosure, modification, or disruption of applications, sandboxes, disks, credentials, and other managed resources. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.1.

title: cassandra-jdbc-wrapper provides a JDBC-compliant API over the Java driver for Apache Cassandra.
desc: cassandra-jdbc-wrapper provides a JDBC-compliant API over the Java driver for Apache Cassandra. Prior to 4.16.4 and 5.0.2, DriverUtil.toStringWithoutSensitiveValues() and DriverUtil.redactSensitiveValuesInJdbcUrl() redact the password property but not the equally sensitive token property used for DataStax Astra and other token-based authentication. When DEBUG logging is enabled, SessionHolder passes connection properties and JDBC URLs containing token through these helpers, causing the live token to be written in plaintext when connections are acquired or released. An attacker who can read those logs can use the token to access Cassandra data and operations authorized to that credential. This issue is fixed in versions 4.16.4 and 5.0.2.

title: mssql-mcp-core is the shared library that powers MSSQL MCP servers.
desc: mssql-mcp-core is the shared library that powers MSSQL MCP servers. Prior to core and server 0.6.0 and reader and writer 0.5.0, multiple database tools interpolate caller-controlled identifiers and predicates into T-SQL batches passed to Request.query() while parameterizing only data values. update_data, delete_data, insert_data, execute_transaction, create_table, create_index, and drop_table accept unsafe tableName, column, index, schema, or free-form whereClause input, while reader-tier list_databases interpolates stateFilter without runtime allowlist enforcement. Row-count and preview queries execute before confirmUpdate or confirmDelete, allowing malicious arguments to bypass confirmation and maxRows controls and execute stacked DDL or DML, read or destroy data, and potentially run operating-system commands when the SQL login is privileged and xp_cmdshell is enabled. This issue is fixed in core and server version 0.6.0 and reader and writer version 0.5.0.

title: The Elementor Website Builder – More Than Just a Page Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 4.0.5 via…
desc: The Elementor Website Builder – More Than Just a Page Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 4.0.5 via `/wp-json/elementor/v1/user` REST endpoint. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Contributor-level access and above, to extract sensitive data including emails, password hashes and usernames for all WordPress users.

title: The failed-login limiter of the JTL-Wawi synchronisation interface of JTL-Shop derives the client identity from the client-controlled X-Forwarded-For header and counts requests…
desc:
The failed-login limiter of the JTL-Wawi
synchronisation interface of JTL-Shop derives the client identity from the
client-controlled X-Forwarded-For header and counts requests without credentials as failed
logins. An unauthenticated remote attacker can block the synchronisation
between JTL-Shop and JTL-Wawi with a few requests and repeat this
indefinitely, so that orders are no longer handed over to JTL-Wawi. No data is disclosed
and no code is executed.

title: Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fail to limit the aggregate memory allocated when processing ZIP archive entries during document…
desc: Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fail to limit the aggregate memory allocated when processing ZIP archive entries during document content extraction and Slack workspace import, which allows an authenticated attacker to cause a server-side denial of service via a crafted ZIP archive.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00772

title: Cross-site scripting in the embedded co-browsing feature in Unblu inc.
desc:
Cross-site scripting in the embedded co-browsing feature in Unblu inc. Unblu Spark 7.0 through 7.57.9 and 8.0 before 8.40.2, on on-premises and cloud deployments, allows an unauthenticated remote attacker in the visitor role to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of an agent taking part in the attacker's co-browsing session, via manipulated synchronized page attributes of the co-browsed page.



The JavaScript runs in the context and under the identity of the agent's session in the Agent Desk or the Single Conversation Desk.



Exploitation requires an agent to join an embedded co-browsing session with the attacker. Mobile co-apping isn't affected.

title: The WP Duplicate – WordPress Migration Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.11 via the…
desc: The WP Duplicate – WordPress Migration Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.11 via the save_single_batch_file function. This is due to a PHP type-juggling authentication bypass via loose != comparison with no is_string() guard, combined with unsanitized base64-decoded path construction in save_single_batch_file() lacking any directory traversal containment. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with custom-level access and above, to execute code on the server. Exploitation requires that the site owner has completed the plugin's initial setup so that the site_type and prod_key_random_id options are non-empty, though any non-empty secret value is bypassable via the type-juggling flaw.

title: The WP Duplicate – WordPress Migration Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.11 via the 'file_name' parameter.
desc: The WP Duplicate – WordPress Migration Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.11 via the 'file_name' parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read the contents of arbitrary files on the server, which can contain sensitive information. The authentication bypass requires submitting the JSON boolean `true` as the `prod_key_random_id` value, which coerces against any non-empty stored secret so that the loose `!=` comparison evaluates to false, skipping the rejection branch entirely without knowledge of the secret.

title: WebToffee Product Feed before 2.4.4 for WordPress contains a use of hard-coded cryptographic key vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass the URL-cron…
desc: WebToffee Product Feed before 2.4.4 for WordPress contains a use of hard-coded cryptographic key vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass the URL-cron signature check by computing a valid hash using the publicly known constant salt embedded in the plugin source. Attackers can send forged GET requests with attacker-controlled parameters to the unauthenticated init-hooked endpoint to repeatedly trigger product-feed generation, causing CPU/database resource exhaustion and overwriting of the generated feed file.

title: FlowIntel contains an authorization flaw in its duplicate alert ingestion logic.
desc:
FlowIntel contains an authorization flaw in its duplicate alert ingestion logic. When a duplicate alert is received and its content is updated, the ownership and visibility scope fields (owner user and owner organization) were not refreshed to reflect the connector's current scope. As a result, an alert that was originally created under a broader visibility scope retained that broader scope even after the connector's scope was narrowed or changed.

This means that users or organizations that should no longer have visibility into a given alert could continue to access it, because the stale ownership fields were never updated during the duplicate-update path. The issue affected all duplicate updates, including those involving alerts in terminal review states and those recovered from uniqueness conflicts.

Security impact:
- Unauthorized disclosure of security alert content to users or organizations outside the intended visibility scope.
- Stale access persists indefinitely until the alert is independently re-scoped or deleted.

Affected version: <4.1.0.

title: MISP contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the Galaxy import/sync functionality (captureGalaxy in app/Model/Galaxy.php).
desc: MISP contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the Galaxy import/sync functionality (captureGalaxy in app/Model/Galaxy.php). The captureGalaxy() method matched an incoming galaxy payload to an existing galaxy by UUID and unconditionally overwrote the matched record, regardless of whether the importing user belonged to the owning organization or whether the galaxy was a system-provided default galaxy. Any authenticated user holding the perm_galaxy_editor role could therefore: (1) demote a default galaxy by setting its default flag to false, (2) reassign the galaxy's org_id and orgc_id to the attacker's organization, effectively taking ownership, and (3) modify other galaxy fields (name, description, distribution, version). Additionally, the role-level permission check (perm_site_admin or perm_galaxy_editor) was executed after the captureOrganisationAndSG() call, meaning organization and sharing-group data was already captured before the authorization decision was made. The vulnerability requires an authenticated user with the perm_galaxy_editor role and the ability to submit a galaxy import payload containing a UUID that matches an existing galaxy. The security impact is loss of data integrity across the MISP instance: default galaxy definitions are corrupted, cross-organization ownership is silently transferred, and the integrity of shared threat-intelligence galaxy metadata is compromised for all users of the instance.

title: MISP contains an authorization flaw in the GalaxyCluster model's captureCluster() function, which handles the import and synchronization of Galaxy Clusters.
desc:
MISP contains an authorization flaw in the GalaxyCluster model's captureCluster() function, which handles the import and synchronization of Galaxy Clusters. Prior to the fix, any authenticated user holding the galaxy editor role could replace an existing locked Galaxy Cluster by supplying its UUID in an import request, regardless of which organization owned the cluster. The function unconditionally called captureOrganisationAndSG() before the save operation, overwriting the cluster's org_id and orgc_id fields with the importing user's organization, effectively transferring ownership of the cluster to the attacker's organization. Additionally, the save operation was not restricted to a specific set of fields, allowing arbitrary field modification.

The vulnerable behavior required the attacker to possess a valid MISP account with the perm_galaxy_editor role and to know or discover the UUID of a target cluster belonging to another organization. No site-admin or owner-organization privilege was enforced for the update path. The result was that a low-privilege galaxy editor in one organization could modify the content (value, description, distribution, etc.) of clusters owned by other organizations and seize ownership, corrupting the integrity of shared threat-intelligence data across the MISP instance.

The vulnerability was reported by ENISA and CERT.pl. The fix introduces an explicit authorization gate that restricts cluster updates to the owner organization, a sync user who can see the cluster via sharing-group rules, or a site administrator, and enforces a field allow-list that excludes org_id and orgc_id from update writes, preserving original ownership.

title: @fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify.
desc: @fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify. In versions up to and including 9.3.6, middie builds the match regular expression for each path-scoped middleware from its mount path without collapsing duplicate slashes, even when the application enables the ignoreDuplicateSlashes router option. Under that option Fastify's router collapses duplicate slashes in both the registered route and the request path, so a mount path containing a doubled slash is served by the router at its single-slash form while the middleware's compiled match still requires the doubled slash and never matches. A path-scoped middleware such as authentication, authorization, or rate limiting is therefore skipped while the router dispatches the request to the protected handler, without any authentication required. Applications are affected when they enable ignoreDuplicateSlashes and a middleware mount path reaches middie with a duplicate slash, most commonly when a plugin prefix that ends with a slash is joined to a mount path that starts with one. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.7, and users should upgrade to 9.3.7 or later. As a workaround, enforce authorization in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after routing, and avoid mount paths and plugin prefixes that introduce duplicate slashes.

title: @fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify.
desc: @fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify. In versions 8.3.0 through 9.3.6, the internal helper that normalizes a path-scoped middleware's mount path only handles string inputs, but the use method also accepts an array of mount paths and passes it through unchanged, so the normalization silently does nothing. As a result, a trailing slash on an array element survives into the generated route-matching regular expression, and an element that is exactly the root path, meaning a catch-all mount, is dropped entirely. Requests to subroutes of the affected mount paths then skip the path-scoped middleware, such as authentication, authorization, or rate limiting, while Fastify's router still dispatches them to the handler, allowing an unauthenticated client to reach protected routes. Applications are affected when they mount middleware on an array of paths in which an element ends with a slash, including one introduced by a plugin prefix that ends with a slash, or is exactly the root path. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.7, and users should upgrade to 9.3.7 or later. As a workaround, enforce authorization in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after routing, and avoid array mount paths with a trailing slash element for security relevant middleware.

title: @fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify.
desc: @fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify. In versions up to and including 9.3.6, middie does not honor the router's caseSensitive setting and matches path-scoped middleware mount paths with a case-insensitive regular expression that does not fold non-ASCII characters, while Fastify's router, when caseSensitive is set to false, lowercases the request path with a Unicode-aware conversion that maps the KELVIN SIGN character (U+212A) to the ASCII letter k. A request that spells a k in a protected mount path as the percent-encoded KELVIN SIGN is therefore routed to the protected handler while the middleware mounted on that path, such as authentication, authorization, or rate limiting, never matches and is skipped, letting an unauthenticated client reach the handler. Only applications that set caseSensitive to false and protect a mount path containing the letter k are affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.7, and users should upgrade to 9.3.7 or later. As a workaround, enforce authorization in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after routing, or keep routing case-sensitive, which is the default.

title: In Eclipse Yasson versions 3.0 to 3.0.5, a race condition (CWE-362) exists in the handling of @JsonbNumberFormat.
desc: In Eclipse Yasson versions 3.0 to 3.0.5, a race condition (CWE-362) exists in the handling of @JsonbNumberFormat. Yasson creates one java.text.NumberFormat instance per annotated property and shares it across all threads that use the same Jsonb instance. NumberFormat is not thread-safe, and the deserializer called parse() on it without synchronization. When multiple threads deserialize concurrently, a thread can receive a numeric value that belongs to another thread's input, receive an incorrect value, or fail with an exception. A remote attacker who can send concurrent requests to an application that deserializes untrusted JSON this way may cause incorrect data to be processed or cause another user's value to be returned. Exploitation requires that the application use @JsonbNumberFormat with a shared Jsonb instance and that the attacker win a timing race. This issue is fixed in version 3.0.6 by synchronizing access to the shared NumberFormat instances.

account. As the IDs are sequential, addresses can be enumerated. Goods may
also be shipped to the wrong address.

desc: The WP-Slimbox2 Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.3.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. title: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity vulnerability in benoitc idna allows an attacker who controls a hostname passed to the library to exhaust CPU via an over-long xn-- label.
desc:
Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity vulnerability in benoitc idna allows an attacker who controls a hostname passed to the library to exhaust CPU via an over-long xn-- label. idna:ulabel/1 in src/idna.erl hands every ASCII label that starts with xn-- to punycode:decode/1 without applying check_label_length/1, the 63-octet DNS label limit. punycode:decode/1 in src/punycode.erl builds its output with list appends in insert/4, so its cost grows super-linearly with the label length. A label of a few kilobytes keeps a scheduler busy for seconds to minutes before the label is rejected as invalid punycode.

Every decode entry point reaches this path: decode/1, decode/2, to_unicode/1 and from_ascii/1. The encode path reaches it as well, because alabel/1 calls ulabel/1 on an ASCII xn-- label before its own length check, so encode/1, encode/2 and to_ascii/1 are affected for such input.

This issue affects idna: from 0.5.0 before 8.0.0.

title: The AIKTP plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authorization Bypass via Predictable Token in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.7.
desc: The AIKTP plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authorization Bypass via Predictable Token in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.7. The vulnerability exists because the plugin's sync token (`aiktpz_token`) is generated using PHP's non-cryptographic `uniqid()` function — producing a wall-clock-derived value with approximately one million microsecond candidates per uncertain generation second — while the unauthenticated, unthrottled REST endpoint `/wp-json/aiktp/checkToken` (registered with `permission_callback => __return_true`) acts as a public brute-force oracle for the token; simultaneously, the capability checks in `check_valid_token` and its wrappers (`verify_aiktp_token_with_edit_capability`, `verify_aiktp_token_with_upload_capability`) inspect only a server-side stored Administrator account (option `aiktp_author`) rather than the actual REST caller, meaning possession of the token alone grants Administrator-equivalent authority to any external request. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to recover the sync token and then invoke `POST /wp-json/aiktp/createpost` to publish arbitrary posts attributed to a site Administrator, `POST /wp-json/aiktp/doUpdatePostWithImageURL` to overwrite the body content of any existing post, and `POST /wp-json/aiktp/doUploadImageToWP` to import remote media and attach it as the featured image of any post. Additionally, when the `aiktpz_token` option has never been initialized, the `checkToken` oracle returns success for an empty token submission due to a loose comparison in `check_valid_token`, providing a zero-effort bypass that requires no brute-forcing whatsoever.

title: The Strava datasource plugin's resource handler POST /strava-api forwards a client-supplied endpoint string, and its query parameters, to the Strava API…
desc:
The Strava datasource plugin's resource handler POST /strava-api forwards a client-supplied endpoint string, and its query parameters, to the Strava API (https://www.strava.com/api/v3/<endpoint>) without validation.

When the datasource is not in OAuth pass-through mode, the request is made with the access token stored on the datasource, not the caller's identity. Grafana authorises plugin resource calls only on the datasources:query permission, which Viewers have by default. Any such caller could therefore request any Strava API path the connected account's OAuth grant allows, for example athlete/clubs or routes/{id}, and read the response.

The plugin's frontend (stravaApi.ts) only needs a fixed set of paths: athlete, athlete/activities, activities/{id}, activities/{id}/streams and segments/{id}.

Requests to Strava are GET only, so the issue is read-only.

Affected: plugin versions 1.2.0 through 1.7.2. The fix restricts endpoint to those five patterns and is pending release. The check runs before the access token is resolved, so a rejected request never causes a token refresh or any call to Strava. Paths with .. segments are rejected as well.

title: The WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro plugins for WordPress are vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 4.17.0 and 6.17.0, respectively, via…
desc: The WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro plugins for WordPress are vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 4.17.0 and 6.17.0, respectively, via deserialization of untrusted input during database restore and staging reset. This is due to the database importer treating attacker-controlled text beginning with {WPSTG_BINARY} as trusted internal binary data and decoding its hexadecimal suffix into serialized bytes. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to plant a malicious serialized object in their own profile. When an Administrator later performs an ordinary database-including restore or staging reset containing that value, and the restored profile metadata is loaded, either during the restore or in a later request, a built-in POP chain can be used to execute arbitrary code on the server. Additional built-in gadget chains allow arbitrary local file read in both WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro and arbitrary file deletion in WP STAGING Pro. The attacker does not require Administrator credentials or a copy of a backup, but exploitation does require the later privileged restore or reset.

title: A flaw was found in libtirpc.
desc: A flaw was found in libtirpc. The SunRPC UDP/datagram server transport reuses a single receive buffer across requests and resets the XDR decode position without rebinding the decode length to the size of the datagram actually received. As a result, when a short UDP RPC request is received after a longer one, the XDR decoder can read stale bytes left in the reused buffer and interpret them as part of the current request, including credential, verifier, or procedure-argument fields. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to data confidentiality and integrity for services that use a UDP-based SunRPC server.
